questions.question: What is the standardization of a random variable $X$ with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma>0$?
questions.explanation: Standardization subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation: $Z=(X-\mu)/\sigma$.
questions.source_support: The definition gives $Z=(X-\mu)/\sigma$.

option_explanations: $(X+\mu)\sigma$ adds the mean and multiplies by $\sigma$; standardization subtracts and divides.
$X/\mu+\sigma$ uses the wrong operations entirely.
$\sigma/(X-\mu)$ inverts the ratio.
